To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the PDBx/mmCF format has been extended to accommodate the needs of archiving integrative/hybrid models, that the IHM-dictionary is a flexible model representation for integrative models that can be used in conjunction with PDBx/mmCDF files, and that PDB-Dev has been created to archive the integrative models in the PDB archive.

integrative models are now archived in the PDB in a format that is compatible with the existing data representation for X-ray and NMR structures, and that the PDB has created a prototype system to facilitate archiving integrative structures.
integrative structural models are now archived in PDB-Dev, and the associated experimental data, modeling protocols, and validation results are available via links to external databases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and implementation of a community-wide standard for the archiving and dissemination of integrative models, and the associated experimental data.
the archiving of integrative structural models and their dissemination via the Protein Data Bank (PDB), the primary repository for macromolecular structures.
the development and implementation of a framework to support integrative modeling and archiving of integrative structures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
integrative modeling is an important new method in structural biology, with a number of software packages and a growing number of structures.
integrative modeling has matured to the point where it can produce high-quality models that can be archived in a manner consistent with existing PDBx/PDB standards.
the PDB is the ideal place to deposit integrative structural models and that the IHM-dictionary is a flexible way to represent them.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have created a new data representation for integrative models, and we have implemented this new representation in the PDB archive.

we have developed a new dictionary for integrative/hybrid models that is compatible with the existing PDB data representation, and have created an archiving system that can store these new models, together with their associated experimental data and model building protocols.
the IHM-dictionary and PDB-Dev have been developed, and the first integrative models have been deposited.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is now possible to archive integrative structures in the PDB and to reproduce the results.

integrative models can now be archived in the PDB in an unambiguous and machine-readable way, and that this will facilitate the development of new tools for the validation, analysis, and dissemination of integrative structural models.
integrative modeling is a mature and important method for solving challenging structural problems.
